expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: Reverse the two string account IDs... Distinguish source and destination at the API boundary if positional calls remain. Use a named command object with validated, branded IDs

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: recursively calls Stripe again without an idempotency key... Require an idempotency key, pass it to Stripe, persist/replay the result keyed to a request-payload fingerprint

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: It then returns `null` for all remaining failures, turning an uncertain financial outcome into a plausible 'no charge' result

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: Floating-point rounding leaks into balances and discounts; `amountCents` has a useful name but is still an unconstrained number

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: `$executeRawUnsafe` is an unnecessary injection footgun... Replace with parameterized query

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: Unknown statuses silently do nothing... Use a closed status union plus exhaustive handling

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: `JSON.parse` accepts untrusted data, no Stripe signature is verified, and no event ID is deduplicated

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: All mistakes framed as actions: 'Send a forged event', 'Run two transfers from the same account concurrently', 'Set `retry` after a timeout'

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Top 3 findings are all 'money movement' category, followed by corruption, reconciliation, entitlement, then irreversible loss

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Each finding specifies exact controls: 'verify provider signature', 'conditional debit in single transaction', 'unique constraint', 'branded IDs', etc.

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: Audit review output only; no code modifications made
